intro: **Tested** means we ran it, and this page says on what, when, and with which version. **Expected to work** means we think it will and have no record of running it. Nothing on this page is a promise.
The automatic tests ran on 5 November 2026, on the exact code in this download.

sections.title: Your Mac
say: Tested on **one Mac**: a MacBook Pro with an Apple M1 Max chip and 64 GB of memory, running **macOS 26.7.2**.
Built for **Apple silicon** Macs. It is not built for Intel Macs.
It asks for macOS 13 or later. **We have not run it on macOS 13, 14 or 15, or on any macOS but 26.7.2.** It may work there; we do not know.
Other Macs and other Apple chips: not tested.

sections.title: Cards and drives
say: Copying to and from **FAT32, exFAT, Mac OS Extended and APFS** was tested.
Those tests ran on **disk images**. macOS mounts a disk image with the same file system drivers as a real card, but a disk image is not a physical card or a card reader.
Used for real, outside the tests, CineSense read cards formatted as exFAT and wrote to drives formatted as exFAT; the last time on 5 November 2026 with CineSense 2.178.1.
Not tested: NTFS drives, network drives, drives behind hubs or docks, and cards in readers other than the ones we own.

sections.title: Cameras
say: **Tested** below means a real card. Each camera is in one group only, the highest its records support.

**Tested on real cards.** Cards from these cameras were copied and checked by CineSense on a real Mac, outside the tests. The date is the last time. This says the card was read, filed by date and verified; it does not say every setting works with that camera.
- **Sony ZV-E1**: Copied and checked once, the last on 2 November 2026 with CineSense 2.178.0.
- **DJI Mavic 4**: Copied and checked 4 times, the last on 5 November 2026 with CineSense 2.178.1.
**Layout read from a real card, not copied.** A camera report from a real card shows CineSense reads its folders and names the camera. No record yet of a real card of these being copied.
- **GoPro Mission 1 Pro ILS**: A camera report from a real card, of 8 October 2026, made with CineSense 2.158.0.
**Tested on test cards only.** Our tests build a card laid out like these cameras'. No record of a real card of them yet.
- Sony A7 IV
- Sony FX3
- Sony Handycam (Memory Stick video layout)
- Nikon ZR
- Insta360 Ace Pro 2
- Canon EOS C80
**Expected to work.** No record yet of a card of these, real or in the tests.
- Sony A7V
- Sony A7S III
- Sony FX30
- Sony FX6
- AVCHD cameras (the PRIVATE/AVCHD layout)
- Sony cameras that record XAVC in the XDROOT layout: from the maker's manual
- DJI Osmo Action cameras
- GoPro HERO13 Black
- Canon EOS C50
- Canon EOS R5
- Canon XF-AVC S and XF-HEVC S cards (XFVC): from the maker's manual
- Fujifilm X-H2S
- Panasonic Lumix S5IIX
- iPhone 15 Pro Max
- Blackmagic cameras (.braw at the root of the card): from the maker's manual
- RED cameras (.R3D in .RDM folders): from the maker's manual
- Z CAM (.zraw): from the maker's manual
Not supported: Panasonic P2 cards, CinemaDNG folders and Atomos recorders.

sections.title: DaVinci Resolve
say: Sending a day to Resolve was run for real in **DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1.0.14**: 2 sends, the last on 5 November 2026 with CineSense 2.178.1.
The automatic tests send into **a model of Resolve built from measurements**, not into Resolve itself. 1380 of those checks ran, and none was skipped.
Other versions of Resolve: not tested.
The free version of Resolve cannot be controlled by other apps: not tested. Sending to Premiere Pro or Final Cut Pro: **not supported**.

sections.title: Cloud copies (CloudSense)
say: Run for real against **Backblaze B2**, **Google Drive**, **Dropbox** and **Hetzner Storage Box (SFTP)**: 40 uploads in all, the last on 27 October 2026.
Not run against a real account: an SFTP server of your own; Amazon S3 and other S3 services.
The automatic tests use a stand-in for every service (rclone v1.75.1 sending to a folder on this Mac). They never touch a real account.

sections.title: How the automatic tests went
say: **80 results on the board, none failed.**
They are the engine's test suites, the app's own self-test (11544 checks), the Resolve colour check, the CineSearch suite and the tidy check.
In all, 21932 checks passed.
No check was skipped.
Run on 5 November 2026, on the Mac above.

sections.title: What was not tested
say: macOS 13, 14 and 15; any macOS 26 other than 26.7.2; Intel Macs; other Apple chips
NTFS drives, network drives, drives behind hubs and docks, physical card readers other than ours
With a real card, as far as the records show: the cameras under Expected to work and under Test cards only
Other versions of DaVinci Resolve
The free version of DaVinci Resolve; Premiere Pro; Final Cut Pro
An SFTP server of your own; Amazon S3 and other S3 services: with a real account
CineSearch (a separate add-on; it gets its own list when it ships)

notes_block:
**Tested on**

Tested means we ran it. Expected to work means we have no record of running it. The full list is in CineSense-2.178.1-tested-on.md next to this download.

- One Mac: MacBook Pro, Apple M1 Max, macOS 26.7.2. Not tested on macOS 13, 14 or 15, on Intel Macs, or on other chips.
- FAT32, exFAT, Mac OS Extended and APFS on disk images. Not on physical cards in every reader.
- Cameras: real cards copied and checked for two cameras (Sony and DJI); a real card's layout read for one camera; test cards only for six cameras; expected to work, no record yet, for 17 cameras.
- DaVinci Resolve Studio 21.1.0.14, run for real; the automatic tests use a model of Resolve. Not tested: other versions, the free version, Premiere Pro, Final Cut Pro.
- Cloud copies to Backblaze B2, Google Drive, Dropbox and Hetzner Storage Box (SFTP), run for real. Not run against a real account: an SFTP server of your own; Amazon S3 and other S3 services.
- 80 board results on this exact code, none failed.
